# Research objective

This project investigates genomic prediction using regularized artificial
neural networks, with emphasis on whether L1 and L2 weight penalties improve
predictive generalization relative to an unregularized neural network and a
GBLUP-ADE genomic mixed model.

The scientific design combines controlled simulation with a planned applied
extension to real *Coffea arabica* genomic and phenotypic data.

# Scientific scope

The validated public analysis currently covers the simulated-data branch. This
branch provides controlled genetic architectures and known true genetic values,
allowing predictive performance to be evaluated independently of the phenotype
used for model fitting.

The study compares GBLUP-ADE with unregularized, L1-, L2-, and L1+L2-regularized
artificial neural networks under the same frozen validation design.

# Why simulated genomic data

The simulated branch contains six scenarios spanning a gradient of genetic
complexity and nominal heritability. Because the scenarios do not form a
complete factorial combination of QTL number and heritability, changes across
the full C1--C6 sequence are not interpreted as the isolated causal effect of
either factor.

The known true genetic value provides a primary evaluation target that is
separate from the observed phenotype. Phenotype prediction is retained as a
secondary outcome.

# Methodological principles

The project follows a common comparison framework across competing methods:

- the same frozen outer-assessment partitions are used for all models;
- model selection and preprocessing are restricted to training or
  outer-analysis data;
- outer-assessment individuals are excluded from ANN hyperparameter and epoch
  selection;
- true simulated genetic values are excluded from model fitting and selection;
- final method comparisons use directly matched held-out individuals.

These principles are designed to preserve separation between model selection
and final predictive assessment.

# Planned Coffea arabica extension

A real-data extension will apply the same separation between data audit,
validation, model fitting, and terminal comparison to *Coffea arabica* genomic
and phenotypic data.

Genotype provenance, genotype quality control, phenotype provenance, and
phenotype preparation will be audited before genomic prediction. This
real-data branch is not yet part of the validated public workflow.

# Reproducible research

The project is implemented in R using `workflowr` and `renv`. Source analyses,
rendered pages, dependency information, and reproducibility metadata are kept
within the same version-controlled research workflow.

The detailed scientific methods and results are presented in the public
analysis modules linked from the project home page.
